finding: An ordinary .git/refs directory can contain a symlinked loose branch ref; Git rev-parse follows the link to read a foreign commit identifier although the top-level .git/refs path itself is not a symlink.

reproduction.type: two freshly initialized disposable Git repositories in isolated Linux test runtime
reproduction.precondition: normal local branch ref resolves to own commit
reproduction.mutation: replace a single local .git/refs/heads/main file with a filesystem symlink targeting the foreign checkout branch ref
reproduction.observed: git -C source rev-parse HEAD returned the external repository commit id
reproduction.affected_existing_guard: old Git isolation checker inspected .git/refs root but did not inspect nested ref files

change: Before any Git rev-parse or Django/PG operation, walk the physical loose refs tree without following links and reject all nested symlink/junction aliases (directories and files), including an over-10000-entry traversal fail-closed bound.

first_party_regression.behavior: Mocks symlink and junction for a nested reference file and directory so Windows does not require symlink privilege; POSIX also uses a physical external-ref symlink.

independent_test_harness.environment: isolated Linux Python and actual local git
independent_test_harness.input: faithful copied production function plus real synthetic Git repos and mocked symlink/junction cases

notes: Do not merge Draft #258 on source guard / isolated fixture results.
